differences: Q01 is dominated by 89.6 Hz with additional 59.7 and 29.9 Hz components, whereas R01 is dominated by 45.9 Hz and has a much broader/higher-centroid spectrum (Q01 centroid 99.29 Hz versus R01 212.52 Hz).

similarities: Both are unclipped, nonsilent 10 s recordings and contain related approximately 30/60/90 Hz spacing families.
Their filter-bank kurtosis is comparatively low rather than strongly impulsive.

similarities: Cepstral signatures are numerically close (distance 0.00189), and both contain approximately 29.9/59.7/89.6 Hz harmonic-family evidence.
Both are stationary-looking, unclipped recordings without detected level changes.

similarities: R04 is the nearest reference in estimator, physical-STFT and reassigned-STFT controls (4.29, 4.17 and 4.19 respectively), and both exhibit persistent tonal spectra with approximately 30 Hz spacing.

differences: R05 is dominated by 43.9 Hz, while Q01 is dominated by 89.6 Hz.

The full-band harmonic structures differ despite shared spacing: Q01 has a dense 29.9 Hz family extending through 568.4 Hz, while R05's prominent family is tied to 29.3 Hz and its dominant carrier tone remains 43.9 Hz.

R06 is dominated by 44.9 Hz with 29.9 and 104.7 Hz secondary peaks; Q01 is dominated by 89.6 Hz with 59.7 and 29.9 Hz secondary peaks.

R06 has substantially stronger broadband high-frequency impulsiveness (kurtosis-bank median 0.352, maximum 1.043) than Q01 (median 0.068, maximum 0.160), and R06 has numerous detected level changes while Q01 has none.

decision.explanation: Initial priorities were the condition-separating low-frequency tone/harmonic structure, cross-carrier envelope modulation, PSD/STFT shape and filter-bank impulsiveness. Q01 is a valid, unclipped 10 s signal, but no reference provides a coherent whole-record match. Its decisive features are the dominant 89.6 Hz tone, strong 59.7/29.9 Hz components, a dense approximately 29.9 Hz family, and carrier-dependent modulation led by 119.4 Hz in 100–500 Hz, 1.12/31.0 Hz in 500–1500 Hz, 120.6 Hz in 4–8 kHz and 89.6 Hz in 8–16 kHz [Q01.C01.S0001, D03.harmonics, D03.envelope_1, D03.envelope_2, D03.envelope_4, D03.envelope_5]. The nearest-reference controls conflict: R06 is nearest in baseline/harmonics, R04 in estimator and STFT views, R05 in modulation map, R08 in envelope band 1, and R03 in cepstrum. Thus the forced rankings do not support acceptance. Strongest counterevidence to a blanket rejection is the shared approximately 30 Hz family across several references, but this is not condition-specific and can arise from related operating frequencies. Orders and synchronous averages are unavailable for Q01 and every reference because no independent RPM trace was supplied [D03.orders, D03.synchronous, R01.orders, R01.synchronous, R03.orders, R03.synchronous, R04.orders, R04.synchronous, R05.orders, R05.synchronous, R06.orders, R06.synchronous, R07.orders, R07.synchronous, R08.orders, R08.synchronous]. No supplied acceptance threshold exists; measurements and the conflicting multi-view numerical controls drive the different result rather than image proximity alone. Fault identity, component and severity therefore remain unsupported.
